creative_extensions.source_label: BLS QCEW Midland County TX (FIPS 48329) NAICS 2111 employment denominator

claims.claim_text: Ring acquired oil & gas properties from Wishbone Energy Partners on April 9, 2019, totaling 49,754 gross (38,230 net) acres on the Northwest Shelf across Gaines, Yoakum, Runnels, and Coke Counties, TX and Lea County, NM.

The acquired properties consist of 49,754 gross (38,230 net) acres and include a 77% average working interest and a 58% average net revenue interest.
claims.subject: Ring Energy
claims.object_value: Wishbone Energy Partners | 49,754 gross / 38,230 net acres

creative_extensions.signal_direction: if Ring is NOT operator-of-record on Wishbone-era leases in the named counties, then operatorship-transfer claim contradicted; presence corroborates the acreage claim

creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: county clerk public records portals; oil-and-gas lease assignment filings
creative_extensions.rationale: Acreage transactions trigger county-level lease-assignment recordings. Direct primary-source evidence of the 38,230 net acre claim, independent of SEC self-disclosure.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: filed lease assignments from Wishbone entities to Ring Energy with effective date 2019-04
creative_extensions.signal_direction: absence at scale contradicts; presence corroborates

claims.extraction_notes: EDGAR FTS will find Ring's own subsequent re-disclosures (8-K announcement, 10-Q references), corroborating the relationship through time. Creative extensions point to TX RRC + NM OCD which would be CANONICAL for this claim type if connectors existed; energy taxonomy has GAP for production_count but facility_scope has EPA primary — EPA is weak for upstream lease acreage (only mid/downstream emissions register).

claims.claim_text: Ring has a $1 billion maximum, $350 million current borrowing base secured Credit Facility with SunTrust Bank (now Truist) as administrative agent, $313 million outstanding as of December 31, 2020, maturing April 2024.
claims.source_quote: On July 1, 2014, the Company entered into a Credit Agreement with SunTrust Bank, as lender, issuing bank and administrative agent... In April 2019, the Company amended and restated its Credit Agreement... increases the maximum borrowing amount to $1 billion, extends the maturity date through April 2024... The latest amendment adjusted the borrowing base to $350 million... The Company maintains a Credit Facility which currently has a $350 million borrowing base. The outstanding balance on that Credit Facility as of December 31, 2020 is $313 million, which will require repayment or refinancing at or prior maturity in April 2024.
claims.subject: Ring Energy
claims.object_value: SunTrust/Truist admin agent | $1B max | $350M borrowing base | $313M drawn

creative_extensions.source_label: Texas Secretary of State UCC-1 financing statement search
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://direct.sos.state.tx.us/ — UCC-1 search by debtor name 'Ring Energy'
creative_extensions.rationale: A $1B-max / $313M-drawn secured-by-first-lien credit facility MUST have a perfected UCC-1 filed in Texas (debtor state of incorporation/HQ). Direct primary-source evidence of the secured-debt claim, bypassing the SEC-disclosure proxy. Real-state UCC is currently a documented PROPOSED connector in the catalog.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: UCC-1 financing statement with Ring Energy as debtor, SunTrust/Truist as secured party, collateral = 'substantially all assets'
creative_extensions.signal_direction: absence contradicts the lien claim; presence corroborates

creative_extensions.source_label: Truist / SunTrust syndicated-loan SNC reporting (Fed Shared National Credit program)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: Fed SNC program (non-public but inferrable from FFIEC bank exam disclosures); Bloomberg LFinance/Loanconnector indices
creative_extensions.rationale: A $1B max syndicated credit facility crosses the $100M SNC threshold and would be reported by SunTrust/Truist in the Shared National Credit program. Not publicly granular but Refinitiv LPC tracks the syndicate.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: syndicate participant list confirming SunTrust as lead + several other banks
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence corroborates real syndicated facility; absence in trackers would be a soft contradiction

claims.extraction_notes: $313M drawn against $350M base = 89% utilization, a real signal of leverage tightness; ucc_proxy via 10-K Notes / 8-K Item 2.03 will catch the secured-debt disclosure cadence. Per H10 discipline: high utilization is one distress marker; need clustering with other markers (see REI-4 sub-$1 equity raise) before firing distress.

claims.claim_text: In October 2020 Ring closed an underwritten public offering of 9,575,800 Common Shares + 13,428,500 Pre-Funded Warrants + 23,004,300 Common Warrants at a combined $0.70 purchase price (sub-$1 distressed equity raise) plus a concurrent registered direct at $0.70.

Concurrently with the underwritten public offering, the Company closed on a registered direct offering of (i) 3,500,000 Common Shares, (ii) 3,300,000 Pre-Funded Warrants and (iii) 6,800,000 Common Warrants at a combined purchase price of $0.70. The Common Warrants have a term of five years and an exercise price of $0.80 per share. Gross proceeds totaled $4,756,700.
claims.subject: Ring Energy
claims.object_value: $0.70 combined purchase price | ~$20.8M gross proceeds | 5-yr warrants at $0.80 strike

creative_extensions.source_label: NYSE American listing standards continued-listing notices (NYSE Regulation)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: NYSE American listing-standards compliance notices + 8-K Item 3.01 filings
creative_extensions.rationale: A combined $0.70 offering price implies the underlying common may have been near or below NYSE American $1 minimum bid price threshold. Listing-deficiency 8-K disclosures (Item 3.01) and any reverse-split S-1/S-3 would be a second distress marker. H10 discipline: a sub-$1 equity raise is meaningful only when CLUSTERED with other markers.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: 8-K Item 3.01 listing deficiency notice; reverse-split proxy materials
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence of multiple distress markers (>=2 of: sub-$1 raise, listing notice, reverse split, ATM, debt covenant amendment) within 12 months corroborates distress cluster

creative_extensions.source_label: iborrow / IBKR securities-lending data for REI
creative_extensions.rationale: Distressed sub-$1 equity raises often precede borrow-fee spikes. Useful corroborating signal post-cutoff would violate hindsight blinding, but the connector can be parameterized at the cutoff date to test whether the FY2020 distress was already showing in borrow markets.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: annualized borrow fee + shares-available trend at cutoff
creative_extensions.signal_direction: elevated borrow fee corroborates distress; benign borrow market is a soft non-confirmation

claims.extraction_notes: Pairs with REI-3 (89% credit facility utilization). Two distress markers within 6 months (Oct 2020 sub-$1 raise + Dec 2020 base redetermination) — meets H10 threshold of 2+ markers. sec_filings.list_filings_by_form will trace 424B/S-3 cadence; UCC proxy (REI-3) catches the secured-debt side. Note: NYSE American (not OTC) — Ring is a real reporting issuer, not a microcap fraud pattern.

claims.claim_text: As of December 31, 2020 Ring had derivative contracts covering 9,000 barrels of oil per day for 2021 (4,500 in costless collars at $52.71-$55.35 ceiling, 4,500 in swaps at $45.00-$45.96) and 1,750 bpd for 2022 — implying operational scale of ~9-10,000 bpd.

For 2021, contracts covering 4,500 of the 9,000 barrels of oil are in the form of costless collars of WTI Crude Oil prices.
claims.subject: Ring Energy

creative_extensions.source_label: TX RRC monthly oil production by operator (Form PR)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://webapps.rrc.texas.gov/PR/publicMonthlyOnlineQueryAction.do — Form PR monthly production by operator number, by county
creative_extensions.rationale: Hedging 9,000 bpd implies actual production OF AT LEAST that magnitude (operators typically hedge 50-80% of expected production). TX RRC Form PR is the regulator-side ground truth for monthly produced barrels — the direct operational-capacity test of the implied 11,000-18,000 bpd total production scale.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: Ring Energy monthly oil production 2020-2021 in the named counties, summed across leases
creative_extensions.signal_direction: if RRC PR shows production << 9,000 bpd then hedging exceeds production (suspicious); if RRC shows ~11,000-18,000 bpd then hedge ratio is normal

creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: 10-K credit-agreement exhibits often name eligible hedge counterparties; cross-check with SunTrust/Truist commodity-hedging desk public mandates
creative_extensions.rationale: Secured credit facilities require hedges to be with approved counterparties; the credit facility lender (SunTrust/Truist) likely is one. Indirect corroboration that the hedge book is real.

claims.extraction_notes: Energy taxonomy has production_count_generation = GAP for power but NOT for upstream oil; the canonical source is TX RRC + EIA Form 914 (states aggregated). claim_evolution test catches whether Ring re-affirms the hedge program in subsequent 10-Q filings (REAFFIRMED vs SILENT). Operational-capacity TX RRC test is the heart of this claim.
